New Orleans.h: Squeezed between Lake Pontchartrain and a big bend of the Mississippi, near where the river reaches the Gulf.

Baton Rouge.h: On the east bank of the Mississippi, where the river leaves the north–south stretch and starts winding down to the Gulf.

Shreveport.h: Up in Louisiana's northwest corner, on the Red River, about 20 miles from the Texas line.

Lafayette.h: In the heart of Cajun country, just west of the Atchafalaya Basin, America's largest river swamp.

Austin.h: In the middle of Texas, where the Colorado River comes out of the Hill Country lakes like Lake Travis.

Houston.h: Near the upper Texas coast, about 25 miles inland from Galveston Bay.

El Paso.h: At the very western tip of Texas, where the Rio Grande meets New Mexico and Mexico.

Dallas.h: In north Texas, about 70 miles south of the Red River, the Oklahoma border.

San Antonio.h: Where the Hill Country meets the south Texas plains, about 140 miles inland from Corpus Christi Bay.

Nashville.h: Right in the middle of the state, on a loop of the Cumberland River.

Memphis.h: In the far southwest corner, on the bluffs above the Mississippi, where Tennessee meets Arkansas and Mississippi.

Knoxville.h: In east Tennessee, about 30 miles northwest of the Great Smoky Mountains.

Chattanooga.h: On the southern edge, right on the Georgia line, where the Tennessee River cuts through the mountains.

Los Angeles.h: On the southern coast where it bends east, around Santa Monica Bay, about 120 miles north of Mexico.

San Francisco.h: On the big bay halfway up California's coast, at the tip of the peninsula between the bay and the Pacific.

Sacramento.h: Inland in the Central Valley, about 85 miles west of Lake Tahoe, where the Sacramento and American rivers meet.

San Diego.h: In the very bottom-left corner of the state, on a sheltered bay right next to the Mexican border.

New York City.h: At the state's southern tip, where the Hudson River meets the Atlantic, right beside Long Island.

Albany.h: On the Hudson River about 150 miles north of its mouth, near where the Mohawk River joins it.

Buffalo.h: At the far western end of the state, at the eastern tip of Lake Erie, near Niagara Falls.

Syracuse.h: In the middle of upstate, between Lake Ontario and the long, thin Finger Lakes.

Honolulu.h: On the south shore of Oʻahu, just east of Pearl Harbor and next to Diamond Head.

Hilo.h: On the wet east side of the Big Island, below the volcano Mauna Kea.

Lahaina.h: On the west coast of Maui, looking across the channel at the island of Lānaʻi.

Kailua-Kona.h: On the dry, sunny west coast of the Big Island, at the foot of Hualālai volcano.

London.h: In the southeast, on the Thames, about 50 miles upriver from where it widens into the estuary.

Birmingham.h: Right in the middle of England, in the Midlands, far from any coast.

Manchester.h: In the northwest, at the western foot of the Pennine hills, the 'backbone of England'.

Liverpool.h: On the northwest coast, at the mouth of the River Mersey, facing the Irish Sea.

Leeds.h: In Yorkshire, on the east side of the Pennines, just southeast of the Yorkshire Dales.

Newcastle.h: In the northeast, on the River Tyne just before it reaches the North Sea, about 60 miles south of Scotland.

Bristol.h: In the southwest, where the Severn estuary opens into the Bristol Channel, with Wales across the water.

Sheffield.h: In South Yorkshire, on the eastern edge of the Peak District hills.

Nottingham.h: In the East Midlands on the River Trent, just south of Sherwood Forest, Robin Hood country.

Plymouth.h: On the south coast of Devon, just south of the wild moorland of Dartmoor, near the Cornwall border.

Norwich.h: In East Anglia, the bulge on England's east side, just west of the Norfolk Broads.

York.h: In the flat Vale of York, about 25 miles southwest of the North York Moors.

Oxford.h: On the upper Thames, at the eastern edge of the Cotswold hills.

Cambridge.h: At the southern edge of the Fens, the flat drained marshland that runs up to the Wash.

Brighton.h: On the south coast, straight below London, at the foot of the South Downs hills.

Southampton.h: On the south coast, at the head of a long inlet just north of the Isle of Wight.

Dover.h: At England's southeast tip, the closest point to France, by the White Cliffs.

Carlisle.h: In the far northwest, a few miles from the Scottish border, just north of the Lake District.

Canterbury.h: In Kent, England's southeast corner, about 10 miles south of the mouth of the Thames Estuary.

Edinburgh.h: On the south shore of the Firth of Forth, the big inlet on Scotland's east coast.

Glasgow.h: On the River Clyde in the west, just inland from where it opens into the Firth of Clyde.

Aberdeen.h: On the northeast coast, where Scotland's shoulder bulges out into the North Sea.

Dundee.h: On the north shore of the Firth of Tay, on the east coast.

Inverness.h: At the northern end of Loch Ness and the Great Glen, where they meet the Moray Firth.

Stirling.h: At Scotland's narrow waist, where the River Forth widens into the Firth of Forth.

Perth.h: On the River Tay at the edge of the Highlands, a few miles upriver from the Firth of Tay.

Fort William.h: At the southwest end of the Great Glen, beneath Ben Nevis, Britain's highest mountain.

St Andrews.h: On the east coast of Fife, the peninsula between the Firth of Forth and the Firth of Tay.

Oban.h: On the west coast, looking out at the Isle of Mull, the 'gateway to the Isles'.

Kirkwall.h: On Orkney, the islands just across the Pentland Firth from mainland Scotland's northern tip.

Lerwick.h: On Shetland, the northernmost islands, more than 100 miles north of the mainland, past Orkney.

Cardiff.h: On the south coast, on the Bristol Channel, with England across the water.

Swansea.h: On the south coast, on a wide bay at the base of the Gower Peninsula.

Newport.h: In the southeast corner, by the mouth of the Severn, where the bridges cross into England.

Wrexham.h: In the northeast corner, right by the English border, just south of Chester.

Bangor.h: On the north coast at the Menai Strait, looking across to the island of Anglesey.

Aberystwyth.h: Halfway down the long west coast, in the middle of Cardigan Bay.

Holyhead.h: On Holy Island off Anglesey's west tip, the ferry port for Ireland.

St Davids.h: At the very tip of the southwest peninsula, Pembrokeshire, beside St Brides Bay.

Caernarfon.h: On the Menai Strait across from Anglesey, at the foot of Snowdon, Wales's highest peak.

Llandudno.h: On the north coast between the Great Orme and Little Orme headlands, on Liverpool Bay.

Brecon.h: In the middle of south Wales, at the foot of the Brecon Beacons mountains.

Carmarthen.h: In the southwest, on the River Tywi, just inland from Carmarthen Bay.

Belfast.h: At the head of Belfast Lough, the inlet on the east coast that faces Scotland.

Derry.h: In the northwest, on the River Foyle just before it widens into Lough Foyle, right by the border with the Republic.

Armagh.h: In the south, about 10 miles south of Lough Neagh, the biggest lake in the British Isles.

Newry.h: In the far southeast on the border, just west of the Mourne Mountains.

Enniskillen.h: In the southwest, on the island between Upper and Lower Lough Erne.

Omagh.h: In the west, in County Tyrone, just south of the Sperrin Mountains.

Coleraine.h: A few miles inland from the north coast on the River Bann, east of Lough Foyle.

Ballymena.h: In County Antrim, about 10 miles north of Lough Neagh.

Bushmills.h: On the north coast by the Giant's Causeway, facing Rathlin Island.

Lisburn.h: About 10 miles east of Lough Neagh's southeast shore, on the River Lagan.

Downpatrick.h: Near the east coast, at the southern end of Strangford Lough, where St Patrick is said to be buried.

Dublin.h: Halfway down the east coast, on Dublin Bay, facing Wales across the Irish Sea.

Cork.h: On the south coast, at the head of Cork Harbour, one of the world's biggest natural harbors.

Galway.h: On the west coast at the head of Galway Bay, with the Aran Islands at the bay's mouth.

Limerick.h: In the southwest, where the River Shannon widens into its long estuary.

Waterford.h: On the southeast coast, on the River Suir just above Waterford Harbour.

Kilkenny.h: Inland in the southeast, on the River Nore, about 30 miles north of Waterford Harbour.

Sligo.h: On the northwest coast, on Sligo Bay, beneath flat-topped Benbulben mountain.

Killarney.h: In the far southwest, beside the Lakes of Killarney and Carrauntoohil, Ireland's highest mountain.

Athlone.h: Right in the middle of Ireland, where the River Shannon leaves Lough Ree.

Donegal.h: In the northwest, at the head of Donegal Bay.

Wexford.h: In the southeast corner, at the mouth of the River Slaney, facing St George's Channel and Wales.

Westport.h: On the west coast at Clew Bay, beneath the holy mountain Croagh Patrick.

Dingle.h: Out on the Dingle Peninsula, the long finger of land reaching into the Atlantic in the southwest.

Mexico City.h: In a high valley in the center of the country, about 40 miles northwest of the volcano Popocatépetl.

Puebla.h: Just east of the two big volcanoes, Popocatépetl and Iztaccíhuatl.

Toluca.h: In its own high valley, just northeast of the Nevado de Toluca volcano.

Cuernavaca.h: About 40 miles west of Popocatépetl, where the land drops into warmer valleys: the 'city of eternal spring'.

Querétaro.h: On the central plateau, just southwest of the rugged Sierra Gorda mountains.

Pachuca.h: In the hills about 30 miles north of the Teotihuacan pyramids.

Tlaxcala.h: Just west of La Malinche volcano, in Mexico's smallest state.

Morelia.h: In Michoacán, about 30 miles east of Lake Pátzcuaro.

Taxco.h: Up in the silver-mining mountains of northern Guerrero, about 40 miles south of the Nevado de Toluca volcano.

Acapulco.h: On the Pacific coast, almost straight south of the capital, around a horseshoe-shaped bay.

Veracruz.h: On the Gulf of Mexico coast, about 75 miles east of Pico de Orizaba, Mexico's highest peak.

Xalapa.h: In the misty hills just east of the Cofre de Perote volcano, halfway down to the Gulf coast.

Guanajuato.h: Tucked in a ravine in the Bajío, the fertile highlands northwest of the capital.

Mérida.h: In the northwest of the Yucatán Peninsula, about 20 miles inland from the Gulf of Mexico.

Cancún.h: At the peninsula's northeast corner, where the Gulf meets the Caribbean, just across from Isla Mujeres.

Campeche.h: On the west side of the peninsula, facing the Bay of Campeche.

Chetumal.h: In the far southeast, right on the Belize border at the mouth of the Hondo River.

Valladolid.h: In the middle of the peninsula's north, about 25 miles east of the ruins of Chichén Itzá.

Playa del Carmen.h: On the Caribbean coast, about 35 miles south of the peninsula's northeast corner.

Tulum.h: On the Caribbean coast, Maya ruins on a cliff at the north edge of the Sian Ka'an reserve.

Progreso.h: On the north coast of the peninsula, the port on the Gulf of Mexico.

Izamal.h: The 'yellow city', about 35 miles northwest of Chichén Itzá.

Ciudad del Carmen.h: On a long island between the Gulf and the Laguna de Términos, at the southwest base of the peninsula.

Cozumel.h: On Mexico's biggest Caribbean island, just off the east coast of the peninsula.

Bacalar.h: In the south on the long 'lake of seven colors', about 15 miles from Belize.

Tizimín.h: In the northeast, about 30 miles inland from the Ría Lagartos flamingo lagoon.

Guadalajara.h: About 25 miles north of Lake Chapala, Mexico's biggest lake.

Puerto Vallarta.h: On the Pacific at the head of the Bay of Banderas, one of the biggest bays in Mexico.

Tequila.h: At the foot of the Tequila volcano, surrounded by blue agave fields.

Colima.h: About 20 miles south of the Colima volcano, one of Mexico's most active.

Manzanillo.h: On the Pacific coast of the small state of Colima: Mexico's busiest port.

Tepic.h: In Nayarit, beside the Sangangüey volcano, about 30 miles inland from the Pacific.

Aguascalientes.h: On the high central plateau, capital of one of Mexico's smallest states, which shares its name.

Zacatecas.h: In the high, dry north-central country, east of the Sierra Madre Occidental mountains.

León.h: In the Bajío highlands, about 100 miles northeast of Lake Chapala.

Lagos de Moreno.h: In the Los Altos highlands of Jalisco, on the old silver road north.

Ciudad Guzmán.h: On the shore of Lake Zapotlán, just northeast of the Colima volcano.

Ajijic.h: On the north shore of Lake Chapala.

Havana.h: On the north coast of western Cuba, only about 100 miles south of the Florida Keys.

Santiago de Cuba.h: On the southeast coast, below the Sierra Maestra and Pico Turquino, Cuba's highest peak.

Camagüey.h: Inland in the middle of the long eastern half, about 50 miles south of Cayo Romano, one of Cuba's biggest offshore cays.

Holguín.h: In the northeast, about 30 miles inland from Bariay Bay, where Columbus first landed in Cuba.

Santa Clara.h: In the center of the island, just north of the Escambray Mountains.

Cienfuegos.h: On a big bay on the south coast, about 45 miles east of the Bay of Pigs.

Trinidad.h: On the south coast, at the foot of the Escambray Mountains.

Matanzas.h: On a deep bay on the north coast, facing the Straits of Florida.

Varadero.h: On the long, thin Hicacos Peninsula on the north coast, facing the Straits of Florida.

Pinar del Río.h: In the far west, just south of the limestone hills of the Viñales valley.

Guantánamo.h: Near the island's southeast tip, just inland from Guantánamo Bay.

Baracoa.h: On the north coast of the far eastern tip, near the Windward Passage to Haiti.

Bayamo.h: In the east, on the plains north of the Sierra Maestra and Pico Turquino.

Kingston.h: On the southeast coast, at a big natural harbor below the Blue Mountains.

Montego Bay.h: On the northwest coast, facing the open Caribbean toward Cuba.

Ocho Rios.h: In the middle of the north coast, by Dunn's River Falls.

Negril.h: At the island's far western tip, along Seven Mile Beach.

Port Antonio.h: On the northeast coast, on the far side of the Blue Mountains.

Spanish Town.h: On the southern plains on the Rio Cobre, inland from Portland Bight: the old Spanish capital.

Mandeville.h: High in the hilly center-west, just east of the Santa Cruz Mountains.

May Pen.h: On the southern plains on the Rio Minho, just inland from Portland Bight.

Falmouth.h: On the north coast, beside the glowing Luminous Lagoon.

Port Royal.h: At the end of the long Palisadoes sandspit on the southeast coast, the old pirate capital.

Black River.h: On the southwest coast at the mouth of the Black River, next to the Great Morass wetland.

Morant Bay.h: Near the southeast tip, south of the Blue Mountains.

San Juan.h: On the north coast near the east end, facing the Atlantic Ocean.

Ponce.h: In the middle of the south coast, facing the Caribbean.

Mayagüez.h: On the west coast, facing the Mona Passage toward the Dominican Republic.

Arecibo.h: On the north coast west of the middle; the famous Arecibo radio telescope was just inland.

Caguas.h: In a valley in the east-central interior, about 20 miles southwest of the El Yunque rainforest.

Bayamón.h: On the north coast plain, just inland from the Atlantic, east of the island's middle.

Fajardo.h: At the island's northeast corner, the ferry port for the island of Culebra.

Aguadilla.h: At the island's northwest corner, where the Atlantic meets the Mona Passage.

Humacao.h: On the east coast, south of the El Yunque rainforest.

Guayama.h: On the southeast coast, below the Sierra de Cayey mountains.

Isabela.h: On the northwest coast's surf beaches, facing the Atlantic.

Cabo Rojo.h: In the far southwest corner, by the lighthouse on the red cliffs at the Mona Passage.

Vieques.h: An island off Puerto Rico's east coast, just south of Culebra.
